authority_invariants: One canonical Project Workspace identity and one owner per business fact/rule.
ADMIN publishes reusable policy; USER operates scoped live data; configuration privilege does not imply transaction/approval privilege.
Pinned approved source versions/hashes preserve historical approval; a separate current-readiness check uses existing authority without rewriting those snapshots.
Current source/readiness missing, expired, revoked or stale is visible and blocks only according to applicable governed policy; no silent approval inference.
Canonical activation is not FID and does not clear commitment-only constraints. Legitimate non-Capital-Owner routes use existing route authorization.
No foreign table writes. Owner command may validate/implement authorized cross-domain request, with independent approval where material.
Architecture documents are proposals for future implementation, not business approval or strategic UAT signoff.

p6_manual_schedule_contract.format_asymmetry: Oracle P6 documents XML as supporting baseline import/export whereas XER does not transport baselines in that manner. Prefer XML when baseline exchange is required; an XER current-update exchange needs separate explicitly linked approved-baseline artifact/provenance. Do not claim XML and XER are lossless identical roundtrips.

validation_dimensions: External P6 project identity and canonical Workspace mapping; cross-project/cross-tenant files rejected.
Unique stable activity/WBS/calendar/resource IDs within external source namespace; renamed labels do not create identities; ID reuse/collision explicit.
FS/SS/FF/SF relationship type, lag raw units, predecessor/successor IDs, dangling/external links, duplicates, self-links and cycle warnings/errors under policy.
External project relationships preserved with unresolved dependency marker; do not silently drop or satisfy links outside imported project.
Raw Data Date versus planned/actual dates; missing Data Date not inferred from MustFinishByDate/current date/file timestamp. Date regression/future actuals require documented exception.
Timezone/offset/time-of-day preserved; date-only sources explicitly date-only; cross-timezone display never changes source meaning. UTC audit timestamp separate from schedule working-time basis.
Calendars retain source ID/workweek/shifts/holidays/exceptions/timezone and provenance. No assumed 8-hour day or 5-day week. Unknown calendar/unit blocks conversions needing it.
Duration/work/lag units preserved in raw metadata; any normalization states method/config/hash/rounding and never claims calendar-expanded P6 equivalence.
Constraints, actual/start/finish/remaining duration, percent method, activity codes/resources/load references and imported critical/float values retained with source version.
Cost/resource loads remain imported planning references, not certified actual Cost or native Resource assignment approval.
Quantitative reconciliation: row/relationship/calendar counts, additions/deletions/ID changes and baseline/current/forecast date deltas; unsupported fields/loss visible.
Source file hash, parser/schema/version/config, uploader/reviewer, validation results, accepted version and rollback provenance immutable.

schedule_states.baseline: Approved immutable version; dates represent approved commitment and are changed only by explicit approved baseline revision.
schedule_states.current: Latest reviewed accepted P6 update for a stated Data Date; independent from baseline.
schedule_states.forecast: Explicit provisional or approved forecast scenario with inputs/method; not accepted current nor P6 CPM output unless calculated/imported from P6.
schedule_states.look_ahead: Configurable horizon, default 4 weeks, derived from accepted current plus governed constraints/workfront/material/design/permit/issue data. Does not recalculate CPM.

baseline_and_budget_contract.control_baseline_set: One Project Control Baseline set references separately approved Scope, Schedule, Cost and optional Resource baseline versions and mapping configuration. Partial approval is visible, not collapsed to whole-project approval.

distinctions.original_budget: First independently approved control budget version.
distinctions.approved_budget: A specific immutable approved budget revision.
distinctions.current_budget: Original plus explicitly approved implemented changes/transfers, with lineage; not current forecast.
distinctions.BAC: Approved applicable performance-measurement budget for the control baseline/measurement scope; never automatic equality to FID capital, strategic target, strategic envelope, reserve or cash.
distinctions.actual: Approved certified/accrued economic events for closed/open period under policy; no hidden baseline write.
distinctions.forecast: Versioned future outcome/ETC/EAC derived from explicit source inputs and assumptions.

baseline_and_budget_contract.capital_constraint: FID authorized capital/currency and funding restrictions are upstream constraints; explicit mapping/approval allocates operative control budget. Any mismatch, reserve exclusion, currency normalization or scope difference is recorded; no automatic equality.
cost_policy_requirements: CBS/control accounts/CostCodes, baseline version and many-to-many scope/WBS/activity/contract mapping.
Original/current/forecast/actual monetary basis, currency/FX source/date/hash and rounding; no implicit currency summation.
Contingency and management reserve separate where applicable; drawdown/release needs configured authority and traceable change, no auto QRA output appropriation.
Cost phasing/cash flow independent from strategic scenario/funding coverage; period profile reconciles to approved total.
Approved historical baselines immutable; explicit revision records affected references and decision.

commitment_actual_accrual_contract.gross_commitment: Original awarded value plus approved additive amendments; retain legal obligation history and contract direction.
commitment_actual_accrual_contract.net_open_commitment: Remaining contractual exposure after approved cancellation/closure and recognized fulfillment under configured reservation-liquidation policy. Exact formula must prevent deducting certified actual twice.
commitment_actual_accrual_contract.call_off_po: Declare PO semantics INCLUDED_IN_PARENT / CALL_OFF / ADDITIVE or governed equivalent. Included/call-off PO allocation consumes parent exposure without adding that same value again; additive PO contributes only independent incremental obligation.
commitment_actual_accrual_contract.actual: Certified/accepted incurred economic event, linked to contract/PO/receipt/certificate/source invoice reference and unique origin; not bank settlement.
commitment_actual_accrual_contract.accrual: Explicit estimated incurred-but-unposted/certified obligation for a period, with reversal/matching rule when actual arrives; never add accrual and subsequent actual for same economic origin.
commitment_actual_accrual_contract.deduplication: Source economic-event key + source system/document/line + project/currency/period/reversal provenance; certificate and receipt relating to the same recognized cost need explicit matching, not additive duplication.
commitment_actual_accrual_contract.funding: Strategic assignment/envelope, FBS allocation, gross commitment, net commitment, actual and accrued cost are distinct measures. Do not add allocation/funding rows as obligations.
commitment_actual_accrual_contract.future_interface: Accounting/Treasury supplies posting/settlement references through future authorized interface; current certificates do not claim payment execution.

state_rules: OPEN permits authorized captures and proposed corrections within configured cutoff; source facts retain occurred/received dates.
REVIEW freezes candidate source snapshots for validation/reconciliation; changes return affected owner submission to review with new version.
CLOSED freezes approved progress, reconciled actual/accrual/net commitment inputs and period baseline references; no direct late edits.
PUBLISHED issues immutable report/forecast/input bundle for the closed period; business approval and reporting issuance remain distinct.
Late data uses explicit adjustment/reopen authority; reopening creates auditable new period revision and recalculated report version, preserving published prior version.
One shared reporting calendar/cutoff policy; source-specific transaction dates and P6 Data Date remain distinct, linked rather than forced equal.
Forecast cycle references closed/open source status, assumptions and date; mixed cutoffs disclose exceptions instead of blending silently.
controls: Named period coordinator and source owners
No period or events created by this architecture increment

rules: Source owner emits only after its authorized successful transaction; no event claims approval that did not occur.
One semantic event per aggregate version/idempotency key; idempotent consumers record receipt and reject incompatible replay.
No mutable transaction payload duplication as another source of truth; references and minimum immutable event facts only.
Check tenant/project scope, permissions, version and applicable conditions at owner command boundary.
Start with domain/audit records and explicit service calls inside modular monolith; no event bus/microservice migration proposed.
No events emitted in this architecture increment.

events.authority_limit: Includes source/P6 revision/file hash/data date; does not itself approve baseline or calculate CPM

events.name: PROGRESS_PERIOD_CLOSED
events.trigger: Approved progress frozen under common control period
events.authority_limit: Method/source/denominator/unit/period and revisions; no rewrite on late entry

events.name: CHANGE_SUBMITTED
events.authority_limit: Not approved; no source baseline mutation

events.name: CHANGE_APPROVED

events.authority_limit: No investment authorization or approved source-baseline rewrite

security_and_sod.rbac: Reuse existing tenant/Workspace-scoped permission catalog, role assignments and module/operation checks. Candidate domain roles are scoped duties, not new global super-roles. ADMIN configuration publication and USER transaction authority remain independent.
security_and_sod.read_boundary: Every read/export/report validates tenant, canonical Workspace scope, optional module enablement and sensitive document access; reports do not bypass source access.
security_and_sod.command_boundary: Owner validates canonical active lifecycle, applicable route authorization, condition blockers, exact source revision/ETag, current configuration, role/action and idempotency. Long-running/staged actions revalidate before promotion.

sod.rule: Preparer cannot approve own material baseline; source owners implement only approved versions.
Simple draft entry does not need four-eyes; approved earned/physical reporting does.
Authority thresholds/scope and affected owner receipts; submission not implementation.
Approved assumptions/inputs frozen; no authorization to rewrite baseline.
Highest score is not approval; applicable Post-FID commitment conditions enforced.
Entitlement/quantum/release decision separate from ordinary cost reporting.
Outstanding contractual/claims/financial/handover conditions explicit; canonical identity retained.

primary_source.title: Construction Industry Institute: AWP Overview
primary_source.status: CII overview recognizes CWP, EWP, PWP, SWP and IWP; TWP in this design is project-configured terminology, not asserted universal standard.

awp_optional_contract.activation: Enable by Project Type/execution strategy and published package/readiness configuration; optional for every governance model, never mandatory for all projects.

typed_relationships.rule: Area decomposition and construction package containment, configurable granularity.
Engineering package is supporting prerequisite/many-to-many dependency, not compulsory child in a sequential ladder.
Procurement/material package readiness supports construction; engineering/procurement dependencies may proceed in parallel.
Installation package groups executable scope/activities/quantities, crew/workfront, constraints and release evidence.
Only applicable engineering/material constraints block release; partial/conditional release requires configured authority.
TWP meaning and acceptance evidence must be published by project configuration; may span several packages/systems and is not a universal child of IWP.

awp_optional_contract.release: Readiness combines approved scope, current schedule/look-ahead, available materials, accepted technical revisions, permits/HSE/quality constraints and issues. Package release consumes source evidence and does not resolve source constraints locally.

roadmap.no_calendar_estimate: Complexity is relative architectural judgement; no committed dates, cost or staffing estimates.
roadmap.global_entry: Architecture/domain boundaries and next implementation scope approved. Design/preparation may proceed while strategic business signoff remains paused, but no live deployment/business release without required authorized signoff/release and applicable project authorization.

waves.name: PROJECT CONTROLS FOUNDATION
scope: O1A canonical identity binding and common period/policy first
O1A/O1B minimal document/evidence version references reused before any baseline approval; richer review/distribution/DMS integration remains O2
O1B approved Scope/Schedule/Cost baselines, adapters, typed Progress and Change/Risk/Issue foundation
O1C governed Forecast and source-consuming reporting
dependencies: Existing canonical creation/initialization/activation and scoped security
Explicit decision resolving projects.id versus canonical Workspace references
entry_criteria: Three route applicability and identity collision/access tests specified
No business signoff or release inferred from design approval
exit_criteria: Tested canonical binding with no duplicate Project
Immutable approved baseline set and accepted schedule import provenance
Reconciled no-double-count Cost inputs and typed approved Progress
Versioned Forecast/report inputs with independent approvals and scoped access
Authorized business acceptance/release before live use
risks: Legacy baseline overwrite and duration assumptions

subwaves.purpose: Resolve canonical identity adapter, owner boundaries, route authorization/current conditions and common control period/config policy before wider live reuse.
subwaves.exit: Executable approved design/tests for collision/missing mapping/access/status/conditions and period lifecycle; future schema changes explicitly authorized.

subwaves.purpose: Implement narrowly approved source adapters/control baselines and typed scope/schedule/cost/progress/change/risk/issue foundation without native CPM or duplicate source authority.
subwaves.exit: Baseline/version/data-date/unit/mapping approvals; cost economic-origin rules and typed progress invariants verified.

subwaves.purpose: Add versioned forecast and governed Project Controls reporting/look-ahead consuming approved source snapshots.
subwaves.exit: Reproducible ETC/EAC/time forecast assumptions and source references; no dashboard writes or baseline mutation.

waves.stop_now: No O1 production module implemented in this increment.

waves.name: PROCUREMENT / CONTRACTS / ENGINEERING
scope: Reuse RFQ/bid primitives with configurable sourcing/award
dependencies: O1 canonical binding/period/baseline and Change foundation
entry_criteria: Procurement versus Contract Administration authority approved
Shared parties and source document references designed
Current strategic commercial/funding references remain upstream
exit_criteria: One PO/Contract authority with legal variation history
No duplicated gross/net obligation or actual/accrual economic event
Engineering/document revisions and interface constraints traceable

Contract-client revenue mistaken for purchase cost

waves.name: CONSTRUCTION EXECUTION
scope: HSE scoped internal capability or external system boundary
dependencies: Package policy and source-owner integration contracts
entry_criteria: Applicable source constraints and release criteria approved
Field evidence/measurement units and method configured
Quality/HSE internal versus external boundary decided
exit_criteria: Approved field progress/evidence feeds Progress once
Workfront/package readiness consumes current source constraints
Inspection/NCR/HSE status does not silently imply another owner approval
Audit/late-period adjustment and independent release tests pass

scope: Project closeout without deleting canonical identity

Distinct claim versus ordinary control transaction authority
System/package handover and residual condition acceptance policy approved

Accepted commissioning/handover with unresolved conditions explicit
Project operational closure approved while canonical Workspace/history retained

roadmap.exactly_one_next_implementation_incremen: WAVE O1 — PROJECT CONTROLS FOUNDATION, starting with O1A canonical binding and common period/policy.
roadmap.stop_boundary: Stop after architecture, inventory, roadmap and artifacts. Wait for explicit authorization; do not automatically implement O1.

adr_convention.observed: Repository documents use global numbered docs/NN-*.md, including ADR titles such as ADR 44/65 and later named Wave titles. Existing maximum numeric prefix is 85 (85-qra-evidence-integration-release.md); 86..97 were free at inspection.
adr_convention.proposal_namespace: Use ADR 86..97 for new proposed documents and preserve aliases ADR-O-001..012 required by the prompt. Status PROPOSED_DESIGN. Do not edit or renumber accepted historical ADRs.

adrs.title: Project identity
adrs.decision: Keep enterprise_workspaces of type project as sole canonical Project identity. Bind existing legacy operational records through an explicit tenant-scoped canonical reference/projection adapter; no second Project master and no ID equality shortcut.
adrs.rationale: Canonical project creation already intentionally creates no legacy Project; operational Contract/PO/Schedule still use projects.id.
adrs.implications: O1A must resolve mapping, collision, missing reference, status, scope and authorization before live reuse. No migration in this increment.

adrs.title: Project Controls integration core
adrs.decision: Project Controls coordinates common period/baseline/mapping and integrates governed source snapshots; it does not own every source transaction.
adrs.rationale: High coupling exists in legacy aggregate router/App; a monolithic controls master would duplicate source ownership.
adrs.implications: Domain-owner command boundaries and typed read models; reporting never writes source facts.

adrs.title: P6 external CPM authority
adrs.decision: Primavera P6 remains primary operational CPM calculator. Design manual XML/XER roundtrip only; no native operational CPM, direct P6/OPC API or silent critical-path recalculation.
adrs.rationale: Existing P6 imports/raw metadata are reusable; QRA elapsed-time simulation is explicitly not P6 operational CPM.
adrs.implications: Full fidelity export is a future validated adapter, not claimed as present. Preserve imported critical/float values and raw calendars/units.

adrs.title: Schedule versioning
adrs.decision: Separate immutable approved baseline versions, reviewed accepted current update, provisional forecast scenario and staged import. Promote by explicit approval/version check; no import-driven baseline rewrite.
adrs.rationale: Existing import/baseline/version primitives coexist with activity baseline field overwrites and date-only conversions.
adrs.implications: Future adapter requires version manifest, provenance/hash, data-date rules, source IDs, semantic reconciliation, rollback by pointer/reversal and retained history.

adrs.title: Scope/WBS/CBS alignment
adrs.decision: Use explicit versioned many-to-many mappings among Scope Item, WBS, activity, CBS/CostCode, budget, contract and package. WBS is a structural source, not the sole identity of all cost or scope.
adrs.rationale: Existing control-account/SOV/mapping primitives link multiple structures; one-to-one assumptions lose valid allocation relationships.
adrs.implications: Map cardinality/units/coverage, allocation denominator and historical mapping revisions; no silent auto-join by label.

adrs.title: Progress architecture
adrs.decision: Keep physical, quantity, milestone, schedule, cost and earned progress as typed methods with source owner, unit, denominator, weight, period, evidence and independent approval where material.
adrs.rationale: Existing record primitives and import percent fields are not interchangeable semantic measures.
adrs.implications: Freeze closed approved progress snapshots; EVM consumes approved baseline/progress and reconciled cost, never mixes percentages silently.

adrs.title: Change cross-domain model
adrs.decision: One Change Event/Request coordinates impact assessment and decision across scope/schedule/cost/resources/contracts/risk/forecast. Owners implement approved changes through idempotent commands; no disconnected approval ledgers.
adrs.rationale: Existing ChangeRequest and reserved per-module change menus risk parallel authority if expanded independently.
adrs.implications: Single approved decision reference, affected source versions, implementation receipts and explicit rejection/pending state; no baseline rewrite on submission.

adrs.title: Forecast architecture
adrs.decision: Forecast is an independently approved versioned derivation of governed snapshots plus explicit assumptions; preserves source baseline/current/actual and P6 CPM authority.
adrs.rationale: Existing forecast_scenarios/control_snapshots can be reused, but a scenario is neither strategic investment approval nor source transaction.
adrs.implications: ETC/EAC and finish/milestone predictions disclose method/currency/period/input hashes and approval. Reforecast creates a new version, never edits approved history.

adrs.title: Procurement vs Commitments boundary
adrs.decision: Procurement owns sourcing and recommendation; Contract Administration/Commitments owns one legal obligation register for Contract/PO/subcontract and approved contractual variations. Cost consumes net obligations once.
adrs.rationale: Two menu concepts currently reserve PO access but one table/API exists; strategy/funding are explicitly separate strategic bounded contexts.
adrs.implications: Do not create new Procurement Manager until duplicate concepts and canonical binding are resolved. Define call-off/included/additive PO, client-contract direction and economic-origin dedupe before rollout.

adrs.title: Owner vs Contractor applicability
adrs.decision: Governance Model is independent of Project Type. Reuse canonical creation/initialization/activation and route policies for CAPITAL_OWNER, CONTRACTOR_DELIVERY and DIRECT_INTERNAL; do not impose Capital Owner sequence by default on other legitimate routes.
adrs.rationale: Existing route adapters and policy requirements already distinguish strategic decision, contract award and direct authorization.
adrs.implications: Operational domain applicability is tailored mandatory/optional/conditional/not-applicable; authorization/conditions remain upstream, no copied local FID.

adrs.title: AWP optional architecture
adrs.decision: AWP is configurable by Project Type/execution strategy, not a universal hierarchy. CWA/CWP containment, EWP/PWP support dependencies, IWP executable scope and TWP configured turnover/test relation are explicit typed links.
adrs.rationale: Existing WorkPackage/constraint primitives can be reused but do not establish a mandatory linear package chain.
adrs.implications: No forced CWA→CWP→EWP→PWP→IWP→TWP sequence. Enforce package readiness and optional engineering/material dependencies by published policy.

adrs.title: Operational checkpoints vs Strategic Gates
adrs.decision: Baseline Approved, Ready to Execute, Workfront Ready, Ready for Commissioning/Handover and Closeout Ready are operational readiness checkpoints; they never substitute for Investment Gate/FID or reactivate a Workspace automatically.
adrs.rationale: Existing Post-FID/canonical lifecycle is distinct and has separate scope/currentness/condition/SoD controls.
adrs.implications: Operational checkpoint approval references source evidence and constraints; applicable authorization checked without new strategic approval authority.
